## What Is an Owens Corning Internship?


Owens Corning’s internship program places students on real engineering, manufacturing, and corporate projects across the company’s four business divisions: Insulation, Roofing, Composites, and Doors. The program won the 2025 Campus Forward Best in Class Award from RippleMatch, recognizing excellence across recruitment strategy, technology innovation, candidate experience, and inclusive culture. Interns receive dedicated mentoring, professional development workshops, and present final project results to leadership. The program feeds directly into multi-year rotational development programs for top performers.

## What Are the Eligibility Requirements?


Owens Corning’s internship eligibility criteria are straightforward but worth confirming for your specific track.


• **Education:** Currently enrolled undergraduate or graduate student at an accredited institution.


• **GPA:** Not officially published; peer building materials companies (3M, Dow, Corning) require 3.0 or above, so aim for that benchmark.


• **Class year:** Rising juniors and seniors are preferred for summer internships; some tracks accept sophomores.


• **Majors:** Mechanical, Chemical, Materials Science, Industrial, or Electrical Engineering for technical tracks; Supply Chain, Finance, Marketing, or IT for corporate functions.


• **Work authorization:** Not explicitly stated; international students should contact talentcentercareers@owenscorning.com for eligibility details.


### Does Owens Corning Have a GPA Cutoff for Interns?


Owens Corning does not publish a minimum GPA requirement on its careers page, which gives candidates with strong project experience or manufacturing exposure a viable path even below a 3.0. However, peer companies in building materials (3M, Dow, Corning) consistently enforce a 3.0 floor for engineering interns. Aim for at least a 3.0 and supplement with hands-on experience to stay competitive.

## What Is the Owens Corning Application and Interview Process Like?


Owens Corning follows a four-stage hiring process for interns, starting with campus engagement before online applications.


1. **Connect at campus events.** Attend Owens Corning information sessions, workshops, and career fairs. The company’s process begins with building relationships through recruiting events before formal applications.


2. **Create a Workday profile.** Visit careers.owenscorning.com and set up your applicant account. Browse the Students section to explore available internship and co-op tracks across all four divisions.


3. **Submit your application.** Apply to specific positions through the Workday portal. Tailor your resume to highlight manufacturing, process engineering, or materials science experience relevant to the target division.


4. **Complete interview rounds.** Expect a process that may include a recruiter phone screen, behavioral interview, technical assessment, and potentially a plant tour. Demonstrate knowledge of OC’s products, safety culture, and sustainability goals.


5. **Accept your offer.** Offers arrive by phone and email. Complete background checks, arrange relocation if needed (OC provides assistance), and review onboarding materials before your start date.


See the full Students page for program details at[careers.owenscorning.com/students](https://careers.owenscorning.com/students) .

## How Do You Stand Out at Owens Corning?


First, reference the company’s unique position as the world’s largest fiberglass composites manufacturer. Connect your engineering skills to a specific product challenge, such as how lightweight composites reduce vehicle weight or how insulation R-values are engineered to meet evolving energy codes. Second, demonstrate knowledge of OC’s sustainability commitments: the company ranked number one on Corporate Responsibility Magazine’s 100 Best Corporate Citizens in 2022 and has been on the Dow Jones Sustainability World Index for six consecutive years. Discuss how mechanical engineering contributes to emissions reduction, recycled content in shingles, or energy recovery in manufacturing. Third, prepare for a plant-based interview by brushing up on safety culture (PPE, lockout-tagout), lean concepts (5S, Kaizen, value stream mapping), and the practical mechanical problem-solving that OC’s manufacturing floors demand.

## FAQ


### Does Owens Corning offer internships for mechanical engineering students?


Yes, Owens Corning recruits engineering interns across its Insulation, Roofing, Composites, and Doors divisions. Mechanical engineering students typically work on process improvement, equipment design, quality systems, and capital projects at manufacturing plants or the Granville, Ohio R&D center. Both summer internships and semester-long co-ops are available.


### How much do Owens Corning interns get paid?


All internships and co-ops are paid positions with relocation assistance when required. No official intern pay rate is published, but peer building materials companies pay engineering interns $22 to $30 per hour. Owens Corning’s 3.7 out of 5 pay-and-benefits rating on Indeed suggests competitive compensation within that range.


### When should I apply for the Owens Corning summer 2027 internship?


Start monitoring careers.owenscorning.com in September 2026. Summer internship postings typically appear during fall semester and fill on a rolling basis. Owens Corning recommends connecting with recruiters at campus events before applying online. Submitting your application within the first few weeks of a posting maximizes your chances.


### Where are Owens Corning internships located?


Most engineering internships are at U.S. manufacturing plants across Ohio, Texas, Tennessee, Indiana, and Missouri, or at the Toledo headquarters and Granville Science and Technology Center. Owens Corning operates over 60 facilities globally, but most intern positions are domestic. No remote internship options have been identified.


### What is the Owens Corning intern interview process like?


Owens Corning follows a four-stage process: Connect at campus events, Apply online through Workday, Interview through rounds that may include phone screens, behavioral questions, technical assessments, and plant tours, then receive an Offer by phone and email. Prepare by studying safety culture, lean manufacturing, and the company’s product lines.


### Does Owens Corning convert interns to full-time employees?


No official conversion rate is published. The careers page states that interns can interview for development programs or additional internships at program end. The structured development program pipeline indicates Owens Corning uses internships to identify early-career talent. Peer manufacturers in building materials typically convert 50 to 70 percent of interns.


### What skills should I develop before applying to Owens Corning?


Prioritize CAD proficiency in SolidWorks and AutoCAD, lean manufacturing fundamentals like 5S and value stream mapping, materials science basics covering polymers and composites, and statistical tools for quality control. Hands-on manufacturing experience, lab research, or engineering competition participation strengthens your application significantly more than GPA alone.


### Does Owens Corning sponsor work visas for interns?


Owens Corning does not explicitly state its visa sponsorship policy for interns. Peer building materials companies generally do not sponsor visas for internship positions. International students should contact Owens Corning’s talent center at talentcentercareers@owenscorning.com or check individual postings for eligibility requirements before applying.
